title: ASP.NET Core Hosting: Kestrel, Proxies, Containers

scenes.line1: How does your app reach users?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how your ASP.NET Core app actually gets served to real users? Let’s break down the hosting stack.

scenes.label: Kestrel
scenes.sub: Cross-platform, fast, and built-in for ASP.NET Core.
scenes.say: First up, Kestrel is the default web server. It’s cross-platform and super fast, perfect for development and production.
But in production, apps usually sit behind a reverse proxy like Nginx or IIS. This handles SSL, load balancing, and security for you.

scenes.title: Docker Deployment
scenes.say: Containerizing with Docker makes deployments repeatable and scalable. Just publish, build, and run your app in a container.

scenes.question: Why configure forwarded headers?
scenes.right: It tells your app the original client IP and protocol, crucial for logging, authentication, and generating correct URLs.
scenes.say: Here’s a common interview trap: why bother with forwarded headers behind a proxy? It’s not just for logs—it’s vital for security and correct behavior.
